extracted.intended_audience: DoD judge advocates, contracting officers, procurement policymakers, affected federal employees/unions, and legal scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and recommended procedural standards for conducting, reviewing, and appealing OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing (public-private/comparative cost) studies within the Department of Defense and military departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of inherently governmental vs commercial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity must be determined whether it is 'inherently governmental' or 'commercial' in nature; an 'inherently governmental' activity is defined as one 'that is so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Government employees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final high-level determinations in the Air Force are made by the Assistant Secretary for Manpower, Reserve Affairs, Installations and Environment, subject to DoD and OMB review; activities determined 'inherently governmental' are not subject to A-76 competitive sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IGCA inventory maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must maintain an IGCA (Inherently Governmental/Commercial Activity) inventory documenting inherently governmental activities, commercial activities, and contracted activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory maintenance is required by the FAIR Act and is the basis for identifying activities appropriate for competitive sourcing studies; the inventory must be prepared and submitted to OMB and made available to Congress and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review and update of IGCA inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must periodically review the IGCA inventory to ensure continued justification of in-house performance, identify additional activities for competition, and validate contract manpower equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air Force commands are required to review 100% of in-house activities at least once every five years and agencies must review and update detailed inventories annually as required by the FAIR Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six major components of the standard cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard cost comparison process generally comprises six components: (1) development of a Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP); (2) performance of a management study to determine the Government’s Most Efficient Organization (MEO); (3) development of an in-house Government cost estimate; (4) issuance of the Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation for Bid (IFB); (5) comparison of the in-house bid against a proposed contract/offer; and (6) the Administrative Appeal Process (AAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies in any component can undermine the fairness and credibility of the cost comparison; each component is important to ensure cost comparison decisions are fair, accurate, and consistent with the Supplemental Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) quality and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS 'serves as the scope of work and is the basis for all costs' to be determined and compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sufficiently comprehensive PWS is essential to ensure the requiring activity receives what it needs and that all costs associated with that need are included and considered by the study; poor PWS drafting is a common source of complaints and protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan / Most Efficient Organization (MEO) soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEO, produced by the Management Plan, should outline new, creative, and innovative ways to perform the work required by the PWS and is the basis for all Government costs on the Cost Comparison Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MEO must be developed to achieve the PWS results; the Source Selection Authority must ensure the MEO's level of technical performance is equivalent to that of the selected contract offer and direct revisions if not equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house Government cost estimate supportability and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government in-house cost estimate must be sound, supportable, and accurately reflect costs for the MEO as the basis for comparison against private sector offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Independent Review Officer (IRO) is responsible for certifying the accuracy of the in-house estimate; unsupported or inaccurate estimates can lead to later protests and undermined decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRO (Independent Review Officer) qualifications and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRO 'should be a qualified person from an impartial activity that is organizationally independent of the commercial activity being studied and the activity preparing the cost comparison.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: API 38-203 provided limited guidance until Interim Change required training; DoD and services may require audit agency involvement (especially in large studies) to ensure impartial and experienced review; insufficient IRO review may create later fairness questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source Selection Authority (SSA) evaluation of MEO and TPP
rubrics_metrics.description: The SSA must evaluate the Management Plan and the Technical Performance Plan (TPP) to ensure the MEO offers the same level of performance as the selected contract offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the MEO's level of performance is not equivalent, the SSA must direct the Government to revise the MEO level of performance; in negotiated procurements using cost/technical trade-off, special care is required to match scopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Performance Plan (TPP) and parity in negotiated procurements
rubrics_metrics.description: When negotiated procurements using cost/technical trade-off techniques are used, the Government must submit a TPP to the Contracting Officer and IRO to ensure comparability with private offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional considerations and requirements apply to negotiated procurements to ensure the MEO is based on the same scope and performance levels as the selected contractor offer; failure to align TPP and MEO creates protest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Appeal Process (AAP) purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAP's purpose is to provide 'reasonable assurances' the cost comparison decision was made in accordance with Circular A-76 and the Supplemental Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each military department establishes an AAP to ensure cost comparisons are conducted fairly, equitably, and according to applicable policies; AAP is the final step triggered by tentative 'winner' announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible appellants and scope limitations in AAP
rubrics_metrics.description: AFI 38-203 defines 'eligible appellants' as civilian employees and/or their union representatives 'directly affected' by a tentative decision, and competing contractors, but the issues that may be raised on appeal are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are limited to: (a) specific errors on line items of the Cost Comparison Form (CCF); (b) instances of the agency's denial of information; and (c) particular incidents of agency noncompliance with Circular A-76 and AFI 38-203; broad policy objections are generally not permitted in the AAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparison Form (CCF) line-item accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals specifically identify errors on line items of the Cost Comparison Form and require that all costs entered be 'fair, accurate and calculated in accordance with Part II of this Supplement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supplemental Handbook and AFI require rigorous line-item accounting; failure to enter or incorrect entry of costs on the CCF is a common substantive basis for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of experienced auditors in IRO/AAP for large or complex studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced auditors should be involved as IROs or as part of the AAP team, particularly for large studies or those employing cost/technical trade-off methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Army, Navy, and Marine Corps call for service audit agencies as IROs in large cases; DoD should consider comparable requirements to improve review quality and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAP Authority proactive error correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAP Authority should be encouraged to review and correct any mistaken item discovered during review regardless of whether it was formally challenged by an interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD Interim Guidance should be amended to make it the AAP Authority’s goal to seek out and correct identifiable errors (though not to require a full re-audit), thereby improving appearance and reality of fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of appeal information and draft decisions to interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal information should be released to all interested parties earlier in the process and draft appeal decisions should be provided for review and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language like OPNAVINSTR 4860.7C and AFI 38-203 should be adopted to require contracting officers to provide copies of appeals to other interested parties and to permit input and review; this can speed resolution and improve chances of resolving in the AAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on outside review and GAO non-statutory protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, employees/unions lack standing to pursue cost-comparison challenges at GAO or in federal courts; GAO may consider non-statutory protests if requested by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper recommends OMB amend the Supplemental Handbook to allow agencies to request GAO consider non-statutory challenges brought by affected employees/unions in limited circumstances (e.g., cost/technical trade-off procurements with more than a threshold number of FTEs) and to request GAO invoke 'express options' for speedier decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing doctrines affecting employee/union challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts and GAO have applied standing doctrines (e.g., 'zone of interests', and the 'disappointed bidder' Scanwell doctrine) to deny employees/unions standing in A-76 cost comparison challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees/unions are often found outside the zone of interests of statutes underpinning A-76 and are not 'disappointed bidders' because the MEO is not a 'bid' or 'offer'; this jurisprudence limits judicial and GAO review rights for employees and unions absent legislative change.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAIR Act requires an agency-level administrative appeal process whereby 'interested parties' can challenge the inclusion and/or omission of activities from the agency inventory listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress included federal employees and their unions in the definition of 'interested parties' for inventory listing challenges at the agency-level AAP, although it remains unsettled whether such inventory challenges can be pursued in federal court.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO not being an eligible 'bid' or 'offer'
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEO does not participate in solicitation and is not considered a 'bid' or 'offer' eligible for award; therefore it does not create the special relationship required by Scanwell to claim 'disappointed bidder' status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characteristic of the MEO is a key factor in denying employees/unions standing as 'disappointed bidders' in GAO and court challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee protections upon outsourcing (right-of-first-refusal and transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: When activities are outsourced, contractors must give affected employees a 'right-of-first-refusal' for employment openings under the contract for which they are qualified; many affected employees may transfer to other federal positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These protections (and GAO findings about variable impacts) are contextual criteria considered when evaluating the fairness and consequences of A-76 decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended thresholds and conditions for granting GAO non-statutory protest access
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested limiting conditions for permitting GAO to consider non-statutory employee/union protests include cases involving cost/technical trade-off procurement methods and studies with more than a specified number of FTEs (e.g., sixty-five FTEs), and use of GAO's 'express options' for quicker resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting access to larger and more complex studies seeks to balance contractor concerns about burdens with the need for external review to assure fairness and the appearance of fairness.
